key_insight: LLM agents often produce near-optimal decomposition solvers, but correct outputs can conceal failures to implement the prescribed algorithm.
engineering_relevance: Reliable automated solver development needs algorithm-compliance checks and targeted error feedback, not just feasibility and objective tests.
method: DecompGym benchmarks 81 instances across nine families: five Benders decomposition and four column-generation families.
Solvers must run within 60 seconds, pass feasibility and an LLM-based method audit, and achieve an objective within 1% of the stored optimum.
Evaluate 12 models with up to ten attempts, comparing independent regeneration against failure-guided reflection.
evidence_signal: Two models solved all instances on their first attempt; reflection converted 66% of retries into successes versus 39% for regeneration, while output-only checks would accept 93 of 108 method-audit failures.
watch_item: Algorithm compliance is assessed by an LLM judge, so audit reliability remains an important validation concern.
paper_title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
